title: Mouse Without Borders: with "Use Service" enabled, SYSTEM instances start but never open TCP 15100/15101
summary: Mouse Without Borders service-mode SYSTEM instances remain alive but do not open their TCP listeners, disconnecting the paired PCs.
next_action: Confirm the desktop-activity gate and socket-reopen path for the default SYSTEM instance before approving the targeted service-mode fix.

judgment.rationale: The report provides a two-version reproduction, normal-mode comparison, same-session check, expected SYSTEM log location, and the precise point where service-instance logs stop. Current code opens sockets from a timer branch gated by GetCursorPos and active-console session checks; the record is consistent with that branch not reaching socket initialization, but does not capture the GetCursorPos result. A focused instrumented check can confirm the proposed fix before implementation.
evidence: The reporter reproduced the failure on PowerToys 0.102.3101.0 and 0.102.2933.0 with Use Service enabled on a per-user installation.
Normal mode on the same PC opens TCP 15101 and 15100, while the default SYSTEM instance stops logging after its first GetScreenConfig and remains alive without either listener.
The reporter checked that the SYSTEM instance uses the active console session ID and has already inspected the SYSTEM-profile Mouse Without Borders log location.
Disabling Use Service and restarting restores listeners and both-direction pairing within seconds.
The report includes a second-PC reproduction, firewall checks, multiple display layouts, two Windows builds, and related issue #49094.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the two targeted startup observations—whether IsMyDesktopActive succeeds and whether Common.ReopenSockets is reached in the default SYSTEM instance—then confirm the service-mode listener fix without requesting another generic archive.

fix_assessment.rationale: The service-instance startup path gates socket initialization on cursor-position/desktop activity and active-console session state. If GetCursorPos reports false for the default SYSTEM desktop despite the matching session, service listeners are skipped; separate network startup from desktop input handling only if that exact condition is confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Allow service-mode listeners to start when the default SYSTEM desktop is active
proposed_fixes.root_cause: FrmScreen.HelperTimer_Tick calls Common.ReopenSockets only when WinAPI.IsMyDesktopActive() and the process session matches the active console. IsMyDesktopActive is a direct GetCursorPos success check. If GetCursorPos fails for the service-started default SYSTEM instance, the instance remains alive but never reaches SocketStuff initialization; the reported log ending before the second GetScreenConfig and before either TCP listener is consistent with this path.
plan: Use an instrumented build to record the IsMyDesktopActive result, current and active-console session IDs, and whether Common.ReopenSockets is reached by the default SYSTEM instance after restart.
If the service instance has the active console session but GetCursorPos fails, separate listener startup eligibility from cursor/input availability for service-mode instances on the intended desktop.
Keep input hooks and secure-desktop interaction guarded by their existing desktop checks; do not broaden service behavior beyond the confirmed default-instance case.
Add a focused service-mode regression that verifies the intended instance opens both TCP listeners while an inactive desktop does not create duplicate listeners.
verification: With Use Service enabled, verify the default SYSTEM instance reaches socket initialization and opens TCP 15100 and 15101 after restart.
Verify normal-mode startup and the winlogon instance retain their existing behavior.
Verify a non-active desktop cannot create duplicate listener sockets or perform input handling.

confidence.rationale: The source contains an explicit desktop-activity/session gate before Common.ReopenSockets, and the reported SYSTEM logs stop before the second screen-config call that occurs during socket initialization. The specific GetCursorPos result was not captured, so the proposed condition must be confirmed.

issue_context.summary: With Mouse Without Borders Use Service enabled, service-started SYSTEM instances stay alive but do not bind TCP 15100/15101, causing an otherwise working pair to disconnect.
known_information: The issue is labeled Issue-Bug and Product-Mouse Without Borders and was last updated at 2026-11-07T03:14:32Z.
The reporter tested PowerToys 0.102.3101.0 and 0.102.2933.0 on Windows 11 builds 26200 and 26300.
The per-user install launches the service binary from the user's local PowerToys directory.
The reporter says the default SYSTEM instance logs one GetScreenConfig completion but no subsequent socket startup, while normal mode logs a second screen-config pass and opens ports 15101 and 15100.
Disabling Use Service and restarting restores listeners and pairing; the reporter says the SYSTEM process session matches WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId.
The report includes checks for firewall rules, security-key format, and one- versus three-monitor layouts, plus a reproduction on a second PC.
inferences: GetCursorPos may return false for the default SYSTEM instance even though its session matches the active console, preventing the timer from reaching Common.ReopenSockets.
A second possibility is that the timer reaches the socket path but exits earlier; the current report does not include the two gate/reopen observations needed to distinguish these.
issue_context.analysis: The service starts the SYSTEM instances, but the service process itself is expected to exit after launch. The relevant socket startup occurs later in FrmScreen.HelperTimer_Tick, which enters Common.ReopenSockets only when WinAPI.IsMyDesktopActive succeeds and the process session equals the active console session. IsMyDesktopActive is implemented as GetCursorPos. The normal-versus-service log boundary and the matching session ID make the desktop-activity check a concrete hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. Related issue #49094 is not a duplicate: it reports service-start permission/configuration failures and socket errors, whereas this report says the service starts and the SYSTEM instances never reach listener startup.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report and confirmed there are no issue comments; the reporter supplied detailed normal-mode and SYSTEM-instance log excerpts but no diagnostic archive.
Read related issue #49094. It remains open but describes a service that fails to start and UseService resetting, unlike the current issue where service-launched SYSTEM instances remain alive.

Inspected Program.Main, InitAndCleanup.Init, FrmScreen.HelperTimer_Tick, WinAPI.IsMyDesktopActive, SocketStuff, and TcpServer. The service instance enters the WinForms event loop; the screen timer gates Common.ReopenSockets on IsMyDesktopActive and active-console session state; socket initialization performs the subsequent GetScreenConfig and creates the two listeners.
Searched current open issues and pull requests for the specific SYSTEM/listener symptom; no matching duplicate or covering fix was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether IsMyDesktopActive returns true and Common.ReopenSockets is reached by the default SYSTEM instance after restart with Use Service enabled
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms whether the reported log boundary is caused by the desktop-activity gate or by a failure after the socket-reopen path begins.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use a build that records those two results for the default SYSTEM instance after restart; the issue already contains the broader service and normal-mode log comparison.

Confirm the SYSTEM listener startup gate

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed normal-mode and SYSTEM-instance comparison, including the matching console-session check. You mentioned you can run a diagnostic build; could it record whether `IsMyDesktopActive()` succeeds and whether `Common.ReopenSockets(false)` is reached by the default SYSTEM instance after restart with Use Service enabled? Those two results will distinguish the desktop-activity gate from a failure inside socket initialization; no broader trace is needed.

actions.label: Reproduce service-mode listener startup
actions.note: The issue has a cross-version repro and normal-mode control; confirm the default SYSTEM listener path before changing service behavior.

reproduce.title: Verify Mouse Without Borders service-mode TCP listeners
prerequisites: Two Windows PCs paired and communicating in normal Mouse Without Borders mode.
A per-user PowerToys installation with Use Service available.
setup: On one PC, start with Use Service disabled and confirm both directions of Mouse Without Borders input work.
steps: Run PowerToys as administrator and enable Use Service on one paired PC.
Restart PowerToys and wait at least three minutes.
Check whether the default SYSTEM Mouse Without Borders instance opens TCP 15100 and 15101.
Disable Use Service, restart PowerToys, and compare the listener and pairing behavior.
reproduce.expected_result: The default service-started SYSTEM instance opens the intended TCP listeners and the PC remains paired, while input to the secure desktop works as designed.
